initial_reflection.summary: The run developed a powerful exhaust-oriented shell and reached Donu and Deca with both bosses substantially damaged, but the deck became very large and attack-heavy. The clearest immediate error was ending a turn at 4 HP with 1 energy while a Defend was legally playable and Donu was attacking. Earlier, the run showed good resource conversion by accepting a profitable curse event and promptly removing the curse in the shop.

lessons.title: Do not pass on legal defense at critical HP
lessons.situation: When at very low HP, an attack is incoming, and a block card is playable with the remaining energy.
lessons.lesson: At Turn 6 of the final fight, play the available Defend rather than ending the turn. Even when the exact incoming damage is uncertain, spending 1 energy on legal block is the safer default at 4 HP; preserve the run first and look for damage opportunities on later turns.
evidence_points: Turn 6 showed HP 4/77, Block 0, Energy 1, hand Defend and Defend, with Donu at 163/250 and Intent ATTACK.
The legal alternatives explicitly included Play Defend, but the chosen action was End turn.
lessons.reasoning: This was a directly actionable survival decision: the hand contained playable defense, the player had energy available, and an enemy was attacking. The following turn began at 9 HP, but the run remained in an extremely fragile state and ultimately lost the boss fight.

lessons.title: Stop adding marginal attacks once the deck has a core
lessons.situation: After acquiring a functional exhaust/draw engine and several strong attacks, especially when the deck is already becoming large.
lessons.lesson: Skip more mediocre card rewards unless they clearly improve the deck's plan. Aim to preserve draw consistency rather than continuing to add redundant attacks; this run should have been more selective after establishing Corruption, Burning Pact, True Grit, Dark Embrace, and multiple strong attacks.
evidence_points: The final deck contained 38 cards, including three Perfected Strikes, two Carnages, two Uppercuts, two Headbutts, two Sword Boomerangs, and two Corruptions.
The run continued taking rewards late in Act 3, including Perfected Strike on floor 35, Pummel on floor 39, Dark Embrace on floor 41, Sword Boomerang+ on floor 46, and Shrug It Off on floor 48.
lessons.reasoning: The final build had a meaningful exhaust/draw shell, but its 38-card size and repeated attack packages made access to key cards less consistent. The repeated late additions were not necessary to demonstrate a damage plan and increased dilution before the boss.

lessons.title: Convert profitable curse events only with a removal plan
lessons.situation: When an event offers substantial immediate gold in exchange for a curse and a shop is accessible soon afterward.
lessons.lesson: Accept the gold only when you can reserve enough gold and a shop opportunity to remove the curse promptly. This run handled that line well: it took the 175 gold, then removed Doubt at the next shop for 75 gold.
evidence_points: Act 1 Floor 2 accepted 175 Gold and became cursed with Doubt, raising gold from 109 to 284.
At the Act 1 Floor 3 shop, the run bought card removal for 75 gold and selected Doubt.
lessons.reasoning: The curse was converted into a large net economic gain without allowing it to remain in the deck. This is a reusable event-and-shop pattern when the route and available gold make immediate removal realistic.

human_feedback: No additional correction. The initial reflection identifies the important causes and reusable lessons for this run.
